knowledge:
- key_parameters: TxDb=A TxDb object containing transcript annotations, which must include 'EXONID', 'TXID', and 'GENEID' columns ;; genomeSeqs=A BSgenome or DNAStringSet object containing the reference genome sequences ;; geneticCode=The genetic code table to use for translation (defaults to 'Standard') ;; performAnchorCheck=If TRUE, validates reference alleles against the reference genome; set to FALSE to skip and increase speed ;; ignoreNonMatch=If TRUE, removes non-matching reference anchor records and continues instead of throwing an error ;; aggregateSamples=If TRUE, aggregates samples cohort-wide; if FALSE, processes on a per-sample basis ;; aggregateWithinExon=If TRUE, places multiple mutations within the same exon on the same mutant CDS sequence ;; aggregateWithinTranscript=If TRUE, aggregates multiple mutant exons within the same transcript ;; ignoreOverlappingMutations=If TRUE, retains only the first of overlapping mutations on the same coding position; if FALSE, throws an error ;; maxDistance=Maximum distance from a known exon-boundary before introducing a novel exon during splice junction modeling ;; skipCanonical=If TRUE, skips known canonical exon-exon junctions during splice junction modeling ;; checkWithinMutantSeqs=If TRUE, checks whether cleaved peptides are unique among all generated variant sequences
- alternatives: Users can generate the ProteoDiscography using pre-generated TxDb and BSgenome objects from Bioconductor/AnnotationHub, or build a custom TxDb from GTF/GFF and reference FASTA files using GenomicFeatures::makeTxDbFromGFF and Biostrings::readDNAStringSet.
- when_to_use: Use this package when conducting proteogenomics studies to detect novel variant proteins or proteotypic peptides from mass spectrometry (MS/MS) data using customized search databases derived from DNA/RNA sequencing data (VCF, MAF, or splice junctions).
- pitfalls: Disconcordance between the reference genome used for variant calling and the one used in ProteoDisco can cause errors; always ensure reference anchors match or use ignoreNonMatch = TRUE with caution. Overlapping mutations on the same coding position will throw an error unless ignoreOverlappingMutations = TRUE. Manually altering or adding mutant records via setMutantTranscripts after variant incorporation might bypass sanity checks and affect downstream functions; manual sequences should preferably be imported using importTranscriptSequences beforehand.

workflows.name: genomic_variants_workflow
workflows.intent: Generate a customized protein database incorporating genomic variants (SNVs, MNVs, InDels) from VCF/MAF files.
workflows.stages: 1. Generate the ProteoDiscography reference database ;; 2. Import genomic variants ;; 3. Incorporate genomic variants into transcripts ;; 4. Export the customized database to FASTA
workflows.code:
ProteoDiscography.hg19 <- ProteoDisco::generateProteoDiscography(
TxDb = TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene::TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene, 
genomeSeqs = BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19::BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19
)
ProteoDiscography.hg19 <- ProteoDisco::importGenomicVariants(
ProteoDiscography = ProteoDiscography.hg19,
# Provide the VCF / MAF files.
files = system.file('extdata', 'validationSet_hg19.vcf', package = 'ProteoDisco'), 
# We can replace the original samples within the VCF with nicer names.
samplenames = 'Validation Set (GRCh37)',
# Number of threads used for parallelization.
# We run samples sequentially and parallelize within (variant-wise multi-threading).
threads = 1, 
# To increase import-speed for this example, do not check for validity of the reference anchor with the given reference sequences.
performAnchorCheck = FALSE
)
ProteoDiscography.hg19 <- ProteoDisco::incorporateGenomicVariants(
ProteoDiscography = ProteoDiscography.hg19,
# Do not aggregate samples and generate mutant transcripts from the mutations per sample.
aggregateSamples = FALSE, 
# If there are multiple mutations within the same exon (CDS), place them on the same mutant CDS sequence.
aggregateWithinExon = TRUE, 
# Aggregate multiple mutant exons (CDS) within the same transcripts instead of incorporating one at a time.
aggregateWithinTranscript = TRUE, 
# If there are overlapping mutations on the same coding position, retain only the first of the overlapping mutations.
# If set to FALSE, throw an error and specify which CDS had overlapping mutations.
ignoreOverlappingMutations = TRUE, 
# Number of threads.
threads = 1
)
ProteoDisco::exportProteoDiscography(
  ProteoDiscography = ProteoDiscography.hg19,
  outFile = 'example.fasta',
  aggregateSamples = TRUE
)

workflows.name: splice_junctions_workflow
workflows.intent: Generate a customized protein database incorporating alternative splicing events from BED or custom splice junction files.
input: validationSetSJ_hg19.txt (Custom text file containing splice junctions)
workflows.stages: 1. Generate the ProteoDiscography reference database ;; 2. Import splice junctions ;; 3. Generate junction models ;; 4. Export the customized database to FASTA
workflows.code:
ProteoDiscography.hg19 <- ProteoDisco::generateProteoDiscography(
TxDb = TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene::TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene, 
genomeSeqs = BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19::BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19
)
ProteoDiscography.hg19 <- ProteoDisco::importSpliceJunctions(
  ProteoDiscography = ProteoDiscography.hg19, 
  inputSpliceJunctions = system.file('extdata', 'spliceJunctions_pyQUILTS_chr22.bed', package = 'ProteoDisco'), 
  # (Optional) Rename samples.
  samples = c('pyQUILTS'), 
  # Specify that the given BED files are obtained from TopHat.
  # Chromosomal coordinates from TopHat require additional formatting.
  isTopHat = TRUE,
  aggregateSamples = FALSE,
  removeExisting = TRUE
)
ProteoDiscography.hg19 <- ProteoDisco::generateJunctionModels(
  ProteoDiscography = ProteoDiscography.hg19, 
  # Max. distance from a known exon-boundary before introducing a novel exon.
  # If an adjacent exon is found within this distance, it will shorten or elongate that exon towards the SJ.
  maxDistance = 150, 
  # Should we skip known exon-exon junctions (in which both the acceptor and donor are located on known adjacent exons within the same transcript)
  skipCanonical = TRUE,
  # Perform on multiple threads (optional)
  threads = 4
)
ProteoDisco::exportProteoDiscography(
  ProteoDiscography = ProteoDiscography.hg19, 
  outFile = 'example.fasta', 
  aggregateSamples = TRUE
)

workflows.name: manual_transcripts_workflow
workflows.intent: Import manually-curated or long-read transcript sequences to check for proteotypic peptides and export to a customized protein database.
input: manualSeq (S4Vectors DataFrame containing mutant sequences and metadata)
workflows.stages: 1. Generate the ProteoDiscography reference database ;; 2. Import manual transcript sequences ;; 3. Export the customized database to FASTA
workflows.code:
ProteoDiscography.hg19 <- ProteoDisco::generateProteoDiscography(
TxDb = TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene::TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene, 
genomeSeqs = BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19::BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19
)
testSeq1 <- Biostrings::DNAString('')
testSeq2 <- Biostrings::DNAString('')
manualSeq <- S4Vectors::DataFrame(
  sample = rep('Validation Set (GRCh37)', 2),
  identifier = c('TMPRSS2-ERG prostate cancer specific isoform 1', 'Homo sapiens (human) partial bcr/c-abl oncogene protein'),
  gene = c('TMPRSS2-ERG', 'BCR-ABL1'),
  Tx.SequenceMut = Biostrings::DNAStringSet(base::list(testSeq1, testSeq2))
)
ProteoDiscography.hg19 <- ProteoDisco::importTranscriptSequences(
  ProteoDiscography.hg19, 
  transcripts = manualSeq,
  removeExisting = TRUE
)
ProteoDisco::exportProteoDiscography(
  ProteoDiscography = ProteoDiscography.hg19, 
  outFile = 'example.fasta', 
  aggregateSamples = TRUE
)
